title: Error orchestration taxonomy and latency polyline dashboard
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Engineers need a single canonical surface to quickly classify and act on inference failures and correlated latency degradations across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Current dashboards show raw 5xx counts or few latency percentiles, but we lack an orchestration-focused taxonomy that ties: (a) trace-level exit reasons (client timeout, runtime timeout, model rejection), (b) queue/backpressure signals (queue_wait_ms, batch_size), and (c) protocol-level codes (HTTP/gRPC).

Goal: Deliver a taxonomy + dashboard set that: 1) classifies errors into disjoint categories (TIMEOUT, OVERLOAD, MODEL_ERROR, PROTOCOL_ERROR, INFRA_FAILURE) with heuristics and trace-hook enrichment, 2) surfaces a "latency polyline" visualization (per-route time-series of p50/p95/p99 with shaded error-band overlays) that highlights where errors and latency co-occur, 3) exposes per-model and per-route regression signals for alerting and postmortem, and 4) produces instrumented trace hooks and pipeline transforms to tag spans with taxonomy_reason.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Taxonomy doc exists with explicit detection rules and priority ordering for conflicting signals.
- Instrumentation (trace-hook) deployed to runtime (staging) that injects span attribute "error_taxonomy" with one of: TIMEOUT, OVERLOAD, MODEL_ERROR, PROTOCOL_ERROR, INFRA_FAILURE, NO_ERROR.
- Metrics pipeline adds a derived metric "inference.error_taxonomy.count" labeled by route, model, region, and taxonomy_reason.
- Grafana dashboard with: latency polyline panel, error-band overlay, stacked taxonomy breakdown, heatmap of error bursts by minute, and per-model rejection trend.
- Automated alert rule: if taxonomy_reason=OVERLOAD or TIMEOUT accounts for >20% of errors for 15m and p95 latency increase >30% vs baseline, trigger runbook.
- End-to-end tests and a codelab for SE/Oncall to validate the workflow.

Design notes / detection heuristics: 
- TIMEOUT: detected when request duration >= runtime_config.request_timeout OR span contains explicit client timeout tag. Prioritize over MODEL_ERROR when both present.
- OVERLOAD: when queue_wait_ms > 99th historical baseline and concurrent_running > capacity_threshold OR when batching reduces below min_batch and queue length builds.
- MODEL_ERROR: model returns structured rejection code (model_error.rejection_type) OR logits/exc outputs that match failure signature (nan/inf/oom).
- PROTOCOL_ERROR: HTTP 4xx/5xx or gRPC codes (UNAVAILABLE, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED) mapped to protocol-level bucket; use mapping table in taxonomy doc.
- INFRA_FAILURE: node OOM, GPU driver crashes, process exits. Fallthrough if lower-level telemetry indicates host health issue.

Implementation plan: 
1) Taxonomy draft + review (Confluence) with examples and false-positive cases.
2) Implement trace-hook changes: a lightweight middleware in runtime that evaluates rule-set and sets span tags. (PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/14255)
3) Metrics pipeline: add transform in telemetry ingestion to compute counts and aggregates (ingestion job config PR).
4) Dashboard assembly: build panels in Grafonnet, import to dashboard repo, iterate with PM/Design for usability.
5) Alerts & runbook: create Prometheus/Alertmanager rules and a dedicated Slack escalation channel + playbook.

Rollout strategy: deploy hook to staging, validate with synthetic traces and live shadow traffic, enable metrics pipeline for 7-day backfill, then enable dashboards for oncall consumption. Gradually switch alerts from experimental->production after 2 weeks of low false-positive rate.

Notes on SLO interaction: We will add a derived SLO exposure metric showing percent of SLI breaches attributable to each taxonomy_reason. This will help prioritize long-term remediation (e.g., autoscaler tuning vs model fix).
